q.en: How can you tell a dragonfly from a damselfly when they land?
q.zh: 当它们落下时，你怎样区分蜻蜓和豆娘？

options.en: They look exactly the same when landed
options.zh: 它们落下时看起来完全一样

options.en: A damselfly folds its wings above its back; a dragonfly keeps its wings stretched out
options.zh: 豆娘把翅膀折起放在背上；蜻蜓把翅膀向两侧伸平

options.en: A dragonfly folds its wings; a damselfly stretches them out
options.zh: 蜻蜓折起翅膀；豆娘把翅膀伸平

options.en: Damselflies have no wings at all, because the book explains damselflies lose their wings completely soon after they grow up and leave the water
options.zh: 豆娘根本没有翅膀，因为书中说豆娘长大离开水后很快就完全失去翅膀

explain.en: The book says a damselfly 'folds its wings together and holds them above its back' while a dragonfly 'keep their wings stretched out to either side.'
explain.zh: 书里说豆娘“把翅膀合拢举在背上”，而蜻蜓“始终把翅膀向两侧伸平”。

q.en: Where do young dragonflies, called nymphs, live?
q.zh: 叫做稚虫的幼年蜻蜓住在哪里？

options.en: In trees
options.zh: 在树上

options.en: In water for one or more years
options.zh: 在水里生活一年或更久

options.en: In the desert
options.zh: 在沙漠里

options.en: Underground, because the book explains young dragonflies spend their early life digging tunnels underground
options.zh: 在地下，因为书中说幼年蜻蜓早年在地下挖地道生活

explain.en: The book states nymphs 'live in water for one or more years after hatching.'
explain.zh: 书里说稚虫“孵化后在水里生活一年或更长时间”。

q.en: About how many tiny sections make up each of a dragonfly's eyes?
q.zh: 蜻蜓每只眼睛大约由多少个 tiny sections（小单元）组成？

options.en: About thirty thousand
options.zh: 大约三万个

options.en: About three thousand, because the book states each dragonfly eye contains roughly three thousand tiny parts
options.zh: 大约三千个，因为书中说蜻蜓每只眼睛大约只有三千个小单元

options.en: About one hundred
options.zh: 大约一百个

options.en: About three million
options.zh: 大约三百万个

explain.en: The 'Super Sight' section says 'Each eye is made up of about thirty thousand tiny sections.'
explain.zh: “超级视力”一节说“每只眼睛由大约三万个小单元组成”。

q.en: How fast can a large dragonfly fly?

options.en: About 5 miles per hour
options.zh: 大约每小时5英里

options.en: More than 22 miles (36 km) per hour
options.zh: 超过每小时22英里（36公里）

options.en: About 1 mile per hour, because the book explains a dragonfly flies more slowly than a person walking
options.zh: 大约每小时1英里，因为书中说蜻蜓飞得比走路的人还慢

options.en: About 100 miles per hour
options.zh: 大约每小时100英里

explain.en: The 'Amazing Flight' section says a large dragonfly reaches 'more than 22 miles (36 km) per hour.'
explain.zh: “神奇的飞行”一节说大蜻蜓能达到“超过每小时22英里（36公里）”。

q.en: The author writes that a dragonfly 'speeds up faster than the world's fastest race cars.' Why use this comparison?
q.zh: 作者写道蜻蜓“加速比世界上最快的赛车还快”。为什么用这个对比？

options.en: To describe what a race car looks like
options.zh: 为了描写赛车长什么样

options.en: To help readers imagine the dragonfly's speed using something familiar
options.zh: 用读者熟悉的事物帮助他们想象蜻蜓的速度

options.en: To show dragonflies are actually slow, because the author's real point is that dragonflies are some of the slowest animals alive
options.zh: 为了说明蜻蜓其实很慢，因为作者的真正意思是蜻蜓是现存最慢的动物之一

options.en: To say dragonflies ride in cars
options.zh: 为了说蜻蜓会坐汽车

explain.en: Comparing to fast race cars helps readers picture just how quick a dragonfly is.
explain.zh: 和飞快的赛车作比较，能帮助读者想象蜻蜓到底有多快。

q.en: The book includes a 'Words to Know' list and a Glossary. What is the purpose of these features?
q.zh: 书中包含“需要认识的词”列表和“词汇表”。这些板块的作用是什么？

options.en: To show the author's name, because the Words to Know page is really where the author signs their name
options.zh: 为了显示作者姓名，因为“需要认识的词”一页其实是作者签名的地方

options.en: To help readers understand difficult or important words
options.zh: 为了帮助读者理解难词或重要词汇

options.en: To make the book longer
options.zh: 为了让书更厚

options.en: To list all the illustrations
options.zh: 为了列出所有插图

explain.en: The Words to Know list and Glossary give meanings of key terms like 'gills' and 'habitat' to aid understanding.
explain.zh: “需要认识的词”和“词汇表”给出“鳃”“栖息地”等关键词的含义，以帮助理解。

q.en: The book says a dragonfly catches prey 'more than nine times out of ten,' while a lion catches dinner 'only one out of four tries.' What does this comparison show?
q.zh: 书里说蜻蜓“十次里有九次以上”能抓到猎物，而狮子“四次尝试只有一次”能吃到猎物。这个对比说明了什么？

options.en: Dragonflies and lions hunt in the exact same way
options.zh: 蜻蜓和狮子捕猎方式完全一样

options.en: Dragonflies are among the most successful hunters in the animal world
options.zh: 蜻蜓是动物界最成功的猎手之一

options.en: Both animals never catch any food
options.zh: 两种动物都从来抓不到食物

options.en: Lions are the better hunters, because the book explains lions are the true champions, catching prey almost every single time
options.zh: 狮子是更好的猎手，因为书中说狮子才是真正的冠军，几乎每次都能捕到猎物

explain.en: The book calls the dragonfly 'one of the most successful hunters in the animal world' because of its high catch rate.
explain.zh: 书里称蜻蜓为“动物界最成功的猎手之一”，因为它捕猎成功率很高。

q.en: According to the 'Do You Know?' section, why do scientists study dragonfly flight?
q.zh: 根据“你知道吗？”一节，科学家为什么要研究蜻蜓的飞行？

options.en: To train real dragons
options.zh: 为了训练真正的龙

options.en: To study the weather
options.zh: 为了研究天气

options.en: To learn how to make better airplanes and helicopters
options.zh: 为了学习如何制造更好的飞机和直升机

options.en: To build faster race cars, because the book states dragonfly flight is studied mainly to design quicker race cars
options.zh: 为了制造更快的赛车，因为书中说研究蜻蜓飞行主要是为了设计更快的赛车

explain.en: The 'Do You Know?' box says scientists study dragonfly flight 'to understand how to make better airplanes and helicopters.'
explain.zh: “你知道吗？”方框说科学家研究蜻蜓飞行是“为了理解如何制造更好的飞机和直升机”。

q.en: What is the author's main purpose in writing this book?
q.zh: 作者写这本书的主要目的是什么？

options.en: To describe only one kind of dragonfly
options.zh: 为了只描述一种蜻蜓

options.en: To inform readers about the amazing abilities of dragonflies
options.zh: 为了向读者介绍蜻蜓神奇的能力

options.en: To persuade people to eat dragonflies, because the author includes several recipes for cooking dragonflies in the back
options.zh: 为了说服人们吃蜻蜓，因为作者在书后附上了几道烹饪蜻蜓的食谱

options.en: To tell a made-up story
options.zh: 为了讲一个虚构的故事

explain.en: The book is nonfiction that teaches facts about dragonfly sight, flight, and hunting to inform readers.
explain.zh: 这是一本非虚构的书，讲授蜻蜓的视力、飞行和捕猎等事实，目的是向读者科普。

q.en: The Focus Question asks, 'What makes the dragonfly an amazing insect?' Which idea does the book most support?
q.zh: 焦点问题是：“是什么让蜻蜓成为一种了不起的昆虫？”书中最支持下面哪个观点？

options.en: Dragonflies are dangerous to humans
options.zh: 蜻蜓对人类很危险

options.en: Dragonflies are boring insects
options.zh: 蜻蜓是无趣的昆虫

options.en: Dragonflies are amazing because of their speed, eyesight, and hunting skills
options.zh: 蜻蜓之所以了不起，是因为它们的速度、视力和捕猎技巧

options.en: Dragonflies live only in Japan, because the book explains dragonflies can survive only in Japan and die in other countries
options.zh: 蜻蜓只生活在日本，因为书中说蜻蜓只能在日本生存，到了别的国家就会死

explain.en: The book highlights their fast flight, huge eyes, and high hunting success as reasons they are amazing.
explain.zh: 书里重点介绍了它们飞得快、眼睛大、捕猎成功率高等，说明它们为何了不起。

prompt.en: What makes the dragonfly an amazing insect? Use facts from the book to support your answer.
prompt.zh: 是什么让蜻蜓成为一种了不起的昆虫？用书中的事实来支持你的回答。

guidance.en: - Flight: among the world's fastest insects—over 22 mph, and faster than race cars when speeding up. - Eyesight: about 30,000 tiny sections per eye; can see in almost all directions at once. - Hunting: catches prey more than 9 out of 10 times, better than a lion. - Movement: controls each wing independently; can hover, fly backward, and upside down.
guidance.zh: - 飞行：世界上最快的昆虫之一——超过每小时22英里，加速时比赛车还快。 - 视力：每只眼睛约3万个小单元；几乎能同时看到各个方向。 - 捕猎：十次里有九次以上能抓到猎物，比狮子还强。 - 活动：能独立控制每只翅膀；可以悬停、倒飞、倒着飞。
